title: Are first impressions really accurate
titleChinese: 人们对他人的第一印象是否准确？
paragraphs: Are you a good judge of character? Can you make an accurate judgement of someone's personality based only on your first impression of them? Ironically, the answer lies as much in them as it does in you.

One of the first people to try to identify good judges of character was US psychologist Henry F Adams in 1927. His research led him to conclude that people fell into two groups – good judges of themselves and good judges of others. Adams's research has been widely criticised since then, but he wasn't entirely wrong about there being two distinct types.

More on that in a moment, but first we need to define what a good judge of character is. Is it someone who can read personality or someone who can read emotion? Those are two distinct skills. Emotions such as anger or joy or sadness can generate easily identifiable physical signs. Most of us would probably be able to accurately identify these signs, even in a stranger. As such, most of us are probably good judges of emotion.

In order to be a good judge of personality, however, there needs to be an interaction with the other person, and that person needs to be a 'good target'. 'Good targets' are people who reveal relevant and useful cues to their personality. So this means 'the good judge' will only manifest when reading 'good targets'. This is according to Rogers and Biesanz in their 2019 journal entitled 'Reassessing the good judge of personality'. "We found consistent, clear and strong evidence that the good judge does exist", Rogers and Biesanz concluded. But their key finding is that the good judge does not have magical gifts of perception – they are simply able to "detect and utilise information provided by the good target".

So, are first impressions really accurate? Well, if you're a good judge talking to a 'good target', then it seems the answer is 'yes'. And now we know that good judges probably do exist, more research can be done into how they read personality, what kind of people they are – and whether their skills can be taught.

vocabulary.entry: judge of character /dʒʌdʒ ɒv ˈkærəktə(r)/ n. 识人能力；判断性格的眼光
vocabulary.example: She has a sharp judge of character and never makes wrong choices in friends.
vocabulary.translation: 她有着敏锐的识人眼光，选朋友从来不会看走眼。

vocabulary.entry: accurate judgement /ˈækjərət ˈdʒʌdʒmənt/ n. 准确的判断
vocabulary.example: An accurate judgement of the situation needs calm thinking and full information.
vocabulary.translation: 对形势的准确判断需要冷静的思考和充分的信息。

vocabulary.entry: personality /ˌpɜːsəˈnæləti/ n. 性格；个性；人格
vocabulary.example: His outgoing personality makes him easy to get along with.
vocabulary.translation: 他外向的性格让他很容易相处。

vocabulary.entry: first impression /fɜːst ɪmˈpreʃn/ n. 第一印象
vocabulary.example: A good first impression helps a lot in making new friends.
vocabulary.translation: 良好的第一印象对结交新朋友帮助很大。

vocabulary.entry: ironically /aɪˈrɒnɪkli/ adv. 具有讽刺意味地；讽刺地
vocabulary.example: Ironically, he became a vegetarian after working as a butcher for years.
vocabulary.translation: 具有讽刺意味的是，他做了多年屠夫后，竟然成了素食主义者。

vocabulary.entry: identify /aɪˈdentɪfaɪ/ v. 确定；识别；找出
vocabulary.example: Researchers are trying to identify the root cause of the disease.
vocabulary.translation: 研究人员正试图找出这种疾病的根本原因。

vocabulary.entry: psychologist /saɪˈkɒlədʒɪst/ n. 心理学家
vocabulary.example: The clinical psychologist offers therapy to people with mental health problems.
vocabulary.translation: 这位临床心理学家为有心理健康问题的人提供心理治疗。

vocabulary.entry: conclude /kənˈkluːd/ v. 得出结论；推断；结束
vocabulary.example: After the investigation, we conclude that the accident was caused by human error.
vocabulary.translation: 调查结束后，我们得出结论，这起事故是人为失误造成的。

vocabulary.entry: criticise /ˈkrɪtɪsaɪz/ v. 批评；指责；批判
vocabulary.example: The report criticises the company for its poor safety standards.
vocabulary.translation: 这份报告批评该公司安全标准低下。

vocabulary.entry: entirely /ɪnˈtaɪəli/ adv. 完全地；彻底地；全然
vocabulary.example: The two ideas are entirely different and cannot be confused.
vocabulary.translation: 这两个想法截然不同，不能混为一谈。

vocabulary.entry: distinct /dɪˈstɪŋkt/ adj. 明显的；清晰的；有区别的；独特的
vocabulary.example: There is a distinct difference between the two species of bird.
vocabulary.translation: 这两种鸟类之间有着明显的区别。

vocabulary.entry: define /dɪˈfaɪn/ v. 给……下定义；界定；阐明
vocabulary.example: It is hard to define success because it means different things to different people.
vocabulary.translation: 成功很难被界定，因为它对不同的人来说意义不同。

vocabulary.entry: generate /ˈdʒenəreɪt/ v. 产生；引发；生成
vocabulary.example: This new policy will generate a lot of debate among the public.
vocabulary.translation: 这项新政策会在公众中引发大量争论。

vocabulary.entry: identifiable /aɪˌdentɪˈfaɪəbl/ adj. 可识别的；可辨认的；能确认的
vocabulary.example: The suspect has several identifiable features, such as a big scar on his forehead.
vocabulary.translation: 这名嫌疑人有多个可辨认的特征，比如额头上的一道大伤疤。

vocabulary.entry: physical sign /ˈfɪzɪkl saɪn/ n. 身体信号；生理体征
vocabulary.example: Rapid breathing is a common physical sign of anxiety.
vocabulary.translation: 呼吸急促是焦虑常见的身体信号。

vocabulary.entry: stranger /ˈstreɪndʒə(r)/ n. 陌生人；外地人；异乡人
vocabulary.example: It's not wise to trust a stranger you meet online easily.
vocabulary.translation: 轻易相信网上认识的陌生人是不明智的。

vocabulary.entry: interaction /ˌɪntərˈækʃn/ n. 互动；交流；相互作用
vocabulary.example: Positive interaction between parents and children is vital for a child's growth.
vocabulary.translation: 父母与孩子之间的积极互动对孩子的成长至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: target /ˈtɑːɡɪt/ n. 对象；目标；靶子
vocabulary.example: In this research, the study target is teenagers aged 13 to 16.
vocabulary.translation: 这项研究的调查对象是13至16岁的青少年。

vocabulary.entry: reveal /rɪˈviːl/ v. 揭示；展现；透露；暴露
vocabulary.example: Her words revealed her true feelings about the matter.
vocabulary.translation: 她的话暴露了她对这件事的真实感受。

vocabulary.entry: relevant /ˈreləvənt/ adj. 相关的；切题的；有意义的
vocabulary.example: Please only provide relevant documents for the application.
vocabulary.translation: 请只为这份申请提供相关的文件。

vocabulary.entry: cue /kjuː/ n. 线索；提示；信号
vocabulary.example: His silence was a clear cue that he disagreed with our plan.
vocabulary.translation: 他的沉默是他反对我们计划的明确线索。

vocabulary.entry: manifest /ˈmænɪfest/ v. 显现；显露；表明
vocabulary.example: Her talent for painting began to manifest when she was only five years old.
vocabulary.translation: 她的绘画天赋在她只有五岁时就开始显现。

vocabulary.entry: journal /ˈdʒɜːnl/ n. 期刊；杂志；学术刊物
vocabulary.example: This paper was published in a well-known medical journal.
vocabulary.translation: 这篇论文发表在一本知名的医学期刊上。

vocabulary.entry: entitle /ɪnˈtaɪtl/ v. 给……命名；授予……权利；使有资格
vocabulary.example: The new book is entitled "Stories of the Ocean" and written by a marine biologist.
vocabulary.translation: 这本新书名为《海洋的故事》，由一位海洋生物学家撰写。

vocabulary.entry: reassess /ˌriːəˈses/ v. 重新评估；重新考量；再评价
vocabulary.example: We need to reassess our marketing strategy after the poor sales performance.
vocabulary.translation: 销售业绩不佳后，我们需要重新评估我们的营销策略。

vocabulary.entry: consistent /kənˈsɪstənt/ adj. 一致的；始终如一的；连续的
vocabulary.example: She is a consistent player who always performs well in every match.
vocabulary.translation: 她是一名发挥稳定的运动员，每场比赛都表现出色。

vocabulary.entry: evidence /ˈevɪdəns/ n. 证据；证明；迹象
vocabulary.example: There is strong evidence that he was not at the crime scene at that time.
vocabulary.translation: 有确凿的证据证明他当时不在犯罪现场。

vocabulary.entry: magical /ˈmædʒɪkl/ adj. 神奇的；有魔力的；迷人的
vocabulary.example: The little boy is fascinated by magical stories about dragons and wizards.
vocabulary.translation: 这个小男孩对关于龙和巫师的神奇故事十分着迷。

vocabulary.entry: gift /ɡɪft/ n. 天赋；才能；天资
vocabulary.example: She has a natural gift for music and can play many instruments.
vocabulary.translation: 她有天生的音乐天赋，能演奏多种乐器。

vocabulary.entry: perception /pəˈsepʃn/ n. 感知；洞察力；看法；认知
vocabulary.example: Our perception of beauty is influenced by our culture and life experience.
vocabulary.translation: 我们对美的认知受文化和生活经历的影响。

vocabulary.entry: detect /dɪˈtekt/ v. 察觉；发现；探测；检测
vocabulary.example: The sensor can detect even the smallest change in temperature.
vocabulary.translation: 这个传感器甚至能检测到温度最微小的变化。

vocabulary.entry: utilise /ˈjuːtəlaɪz/ v. 利用；使用；运用
vocabulary.example: We should utilise all available resources to solve the problem.
vocabulary.translation: 我们应该利用所有可用的资源来解决这个问题。

vocabulary.entry: accurate /ˈækjərət/ adj. 准确的；精确的；正确无误的
vocabulary.example: You must be accurate when recording the data for the experiment.
vocabulary.translation: 记录实验数据时，你必须做到精确无误。

sentences.english: Are you a good judge of character?
sentences.chinese: 你是个善于判断他人性格的人吗？

sentences.english: Can you make an accurate judgement of someone's personality based only on your first impression of them?
sentences.chinese: 你能否仅凭第一印象，就准确判断出一个人的性格？

sentences.english: Ironically, the answer lies as much in them as it does in you.
sentences.chinese: 具有讽刺意味的是，答案既取决于对方，也取决于你自己。

sentences.english: One of the first people to try to identify good judges of character was US psychologist Henry F Adams in 1927.
sentences.chinese: 1927年，美国心理学家亨利·F·亚当斯是最早尝试界定“识人高手”的人之一。

sentences.english: His research led him to conclude that people fell into two groups – good judges of themselves and good judges of others.
sentences.chinese: 他的研究得出结论，人可以分为两类——一类善于自我认知，另一类善于洞察他人。

sentences.english: Adams's research has been widely criticised since then, but he wasn't entirely wrong about there being two distinct types.
sentences.chinese: 尽管亚当斯的研究此后饱受诟病，但他提出的“存在两种截然不同类型”的观点，并非完全错误。

sentences.english: More on that in a moment, but first we need to define what a good judge of character is.
sentences.chinese: 关于这一点，我们稍后再详谈，但首先需要明确什么是“善于判断性格的人”。

sentences.english: Is it someone who can read personality or someone who can read emotion?
sentences.chinese: 这类人是能读懂他人性格，还是能体察他人情绪？

sentences.english: Those are two distinct skills.
sentences.chinese: 这是两种截然不同的能力。

sentences.english: Emotions such as anger or joy or sadness can generate easily identifiable physical signs.
sentences.chinese: 愤怒、喜悦、悲伤等情绪，往往会外显为易于识别的生理信号。

sentences.english: Most of us would probably be able to accurately identify these signs, even in a stranger.
sentences.chinese: 即便面对陌生人，我们中的大多数人也能准确捕捉到这些信号。

sentences.english: As such, most of us are probably good judges of emotion.
sentences.chinese: 因此从这个角度来说，或许我们多数人都是“察言观色”的高手。

sentences.english: In order to be a good judge of personality, however, there needs to be an interaction with the other person, and that person needs to be a 'good target'.
sentences.chinese: 然而，若想准确判断他人性格，不仅需要与对方产生互动，对方还得是“易被读懂的人”。

sentences.english: 'Good targets' are people who reveal relevant and useful cues to their personality.
sentences.chinese: 所谓“易被读懂的人”，指的是那些会主动流露与性格相关的有效线索的人。

sentences.english: So this means 'the good judge' will only manifest when reading 'good targets'. This is according to Rogers and Biesanz in their 2019 journal entitled 'Reassessing the good judge of personality'.
sentences.chinese: 罗杰斯和比桑兹在其2019年发表的题为《重新审视“识人高手”》的论文中指出，这意味着“识人高手”的能力，只有在面对“易被读懂的人”时才会显现。

sentences.english: "We found consistent, clear and strong evidence that the good judge does exist", Rogers and Biesanz concluded.
sentences.chinese: 他们的结论是：“我们找到了确凿、清晰且充分的证据，证明‘识人高手’确实存在。”

sentences.english: But their key finding is that the good judge does not have magical gifts of perception – they are simply able to "detect and utilise information provided by the good target".
sentences.chinese: 但他们的核心发现是，这类人并非拥有什么神奇的感知天赋，他们只是能够“发现并利用‘易被读懂的人’所提供的信息”。

sentences.english: So, are first impressions really accurate?
sentences.chinese: 那么，第一印象真的可靠吗？

sentences.english: Well, if you're a good judge talking to a 'good target', then it seems the answer is 'yes'.
sentences.chinese: 答案似乎是肯定的——前提是你是一名“识人高手”，且你面对的是一个“易被读懂的人”。

sentences.english: And now we know that good judges probably do exist, more research can be done into how they read personality, what kind of people they are – and whether their skills can be taught.
sentences.chinese: 既然我们现在知道“识人高手”很可能真实存在，那么未来就可以开展更多研究，探索他们解读他人性格的方式、他们自身的特质，以及这种识人能力是否可以通过后天习得。
